By Their Leaves

Find out what's eating your plants. Search a host plant — a tree, weed, or garden crop — and see which caterpillars of the U.S. & Canada are documented to feed on it.

Try:
Host records here are documented at the genus or plant-family level from the literature, not verified for your exact garden cultivar — and many caterpillars are picky about which part of the plant, or which region, they'll use. Treat this as a shortlist of suspects, not a confirmed ID. Tap “Photos” on a card to compare markings before you commit.
Data drawn from Shropshire, K.J. & Tallamy, D.W. 2025. “Lepidoptera of North America north of Mexico: An annotated list containing geographic ranges and host plant records.” ZooKeys (University of Delaware). This tool re-indexes that dataset by host plant for field use and adds a plain-English plant name lookup; it is not an official product of the original authors. Host-plant associations reflect literature records only — absence of a species here doesn't rule it out, and a caterpillar's actual diet can vary by population. Records flagged in the original dataset as excluded from North America have been removed; strays, unresolved, and exotic records are hidden by default and can be switched back on above.
